newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Ekran to sell Wembley stake.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Ekran to sell Wembley stake.

text.p: Ekran Bhd, builder of the controversial Bakun hydro-electric dam, said it is proposing to sell its 32.82 percent stake in Wembley Industries Bhd for 284.50 million ringgit.
In a statement to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange late on Friday, Ekran said it was selling the stake to Tiong King Sing to enable the company to focus on the 2,400 megawatt capacity Bakun Dam.
Preliminary work has already begun on the $6 billion dam, which will create a reservoir the size of Singapore in a remote forested area of Malaysia's Borneo state of Sarawak.

The dam has been criticised by environmentalists as unnecessary and ecologically unsound. Foreign investors have been lukewarm over the relatively long payback period and construction risks. The dam is due to be finished by 2003.
The deal to sell 47,417,000 Wembley shares to King was made on Monday, Ekran said.
It said the sale would generate an extraordinary gain of 19 million ringgit and 26 million ringgit at the company and group level respectively for the financial year ending next June 30.
Ekran chairman Ting Pek Khing said last month he would announce a restructuring of companies controlled by him.
Analysts have said he needed to do that after the dismal undersubscription of an Ekran rights issue meant to help finance Ekran's equity in Bakun.
An Ekran rights issue of 257.1 million shares was undersubscribed by 62.77 percent. The results forced Ting to pick up over 90 percent of the unwanted portion for 859.8 million ringgit.
Ekran has a 32 percent stake in the Bakun Hydro-Electric Corporation which is due to list on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange next month.
Ting controls three other listed companies apart from Ekran and Wembley.
They are timber products company Pacific Chemical Bhd, engineering firm PWE Industries and property and timber concern Granite Industries Bhd.
